'''Pablo G. Debenedetti''' is an American and Argentine chemical engineer. He is the Class of 1950 Professor in Engineering and Applied Science, Emeritus, and a professor of chemical and biological engineering, emeritus, at [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pablo G. Debenedetti {{!}} Chemical and Biological Engineering |url=https://cbe.princeton.edu/people/pablo-debenedetti |access-date=2026-04-23 |website=cbe.princeton.edu |language=en}}</ref> He served as Princeton's Dean for Research from 2013 to 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fuller-Wright |first=Liz |date=November 22, 2022 |title=Debenedetti to step down after 10 years as dean for research |url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2022/11/22/debenedetti-step-down-after-10-years-dean-research |access-date=2024-01-31 |website=Princeton University |language=en}}</ref> His research focuses on [[thermodynamics]], [[statistical mechanics]], and [[Computational fluid dynamics|computer simulations of liquids and glasses]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cbe.princeton.edu/people/pablo-debenedetti|title=Pablo G. Debenedetti |website=Princeton University |access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref>

Debenedetti was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2000,<ref name=":0" /> the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2008,<ref name=":1" /> and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pablo G. Debenedetti |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/pablo-g-debenedetti-3sdcbs/ |access-date=2023-08-16 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Debenedetti was born in [[Buenos Aires]], [[Argentina]], in 1953. He graduated from the [[University of Buenos Aires]] in 1978 with a degree in chemical engineering, and worked as a process development engineer at the De Nora Company in [[Milan]], [[Italy]], between 1978 and 1980. He completed his master's degree in 1981 and his Ph.D. in 1985, both in chemical engineering, at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where his thesis adviser was [[Robert Reid (chemical engineer)|Robert C. Reid]]. He joined the faculty of [[Princeton University]] in 1985.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ufdc.ufl.edu/AA00000383/00193|title=Chemical Engineering Education|website=ufdc.ufl.edu|language=en|access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Debenedetti's research focuses on theoretical and computational investigations of the structure, dynamics, thermodynamics, and statistical mechanics of liquids and glasses. He has published over 300 scientific papers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=kK2oqWMAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Pablo Debenedetti – Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref> and a book, Metastable Liquids: Concepts and Principles.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691085951/metastable-liquids|title=Metastable Liquids|date=1997-01-12|isbn=978-0-691-08595-1|language=en|last1=Debenedetti|first1=Pablo G.|publisher=Princeton University Press }}</ref>

Debenedetti has made numerous contributions to fundamental understanding of the microscopic structure of [[Supercritical fluid|supercritical fluids]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Eckert|first1=Charles [[nucleation]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Haji-Akbari|first1=Amir|last2=Debenedetti|first2=Pablo G.|date=2015-08-25|title=Direct calculation of ice homogeneous nucleation rate for a molecular model of water|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=112|issue=34|pages=10582–10588|doi=10.1073/pnas.1509267112|issn=0027-8424|pmid=26240318|pmc=4553815|arxiv=1505.01126 transition,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sastry|first1=Srikanth|last2=Debenedetti|first2=Pablo G.|last3=Stillinger|first3=Frank H.|date=11 June 1998|title=Signatures of distinct dynamical regimes in the the Trp-cage miniprotein|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=113|issue=32|pages=8991–8996|doi=10.1073/pnas.1607500113|issn=0027-8424|pmid=27457961|pmc=4987839|bibcode=2016PNAS..113.8991K |doi-access=free}}</ref> and the structure<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Errington|first1=Jeffrey R.|last2=Debenedetti|first2=Pablo G.|date=18 January 2001|title=Relationship between structural order and the anomalies of liquid water|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=409|issue=6818|pages=318–321|doi=10.1038/35053024|pmid=11201735|bibcode=2001Natur.409..318E |s2cid=4311641|issn=1476-4687}}</ref> and thermodynamics of supercooled water.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Speedy|first1=Robin J.|last2=Debenedetti|first2=Pablo G.|last3=Smith|first3=R. His work has been cited more than 46,000 times.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=kK2oqWMAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Pablo Debenedetti – Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=2020-02-24}}</ref>

He served as the chair of the department of [[chemical engineering]] from 1996 to 2004 and was the vice dean of the school of engineering and applied science from 2008 to 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://research.princeton.edu/people/pablo-g-debenedetti|title=Pablo G. Debenedetti {{!}} Office of the Dean for Research|website=research.princeton.edu|access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref> He was appointed Princeton's Dean for Research in 2013<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2013/04/08/princeton-names-debenedetti-dean-research|title=Princeton names Debenedetti dean for research|website=Princeton University|language=en|access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref> and served in this role through August, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About the Dean for Research |url=https://research.princeton.edu/about-us/about-dean |access-date=2024-01-31 |website=Office of the Dean for Research |language=en}}</ref>
